newsitem.title: CHINA: China to open eight new airports in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China to open eight new airports in 1997.

text.p: China is to open eight new airports and to invest a record 18.4 billion yuan ($2.2 billion) in aviation infrastructure and technological renovation this year, the Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.

Of the total investment, 11.8 billion yuan will come from the central government and the remaining 6.6 billion yuan from regional authorities and businesses, it quoted Chen Guangyi, director of the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC), as saying.
Eight new airports would go into operation this year, including eastern Fuzhou and central Nanjing and Nanning while the construction of five airports would continue, Chen said.
Construction of Shanghai's Pudong airport and the expansion of three other airports would start, he said.

The main structure of the new terminal building of Beijing's Capital Airport and some support facilities were scheduled to be completed this year, he said. The project, started in 1995, is the largest airport expansion project in China, costing an estimated three billion yuan.

Five technological renovation projects set for this year include the expansion and upgrading of a national computerised seat booking system, the flight management system of China Southern Airlines, an approach control center in the southern Zhuhai and a maintenance base for China Eastern Airlines.
China invested 9.92 billion yuan in aviation infrastructure and technological renovation in 1996, a 57 percent increase over the previous year, he said.
